complete: FRAMING CORRECTION: this file is NOT the Listener. It is the shared base + formula library (contract sections 1,2,4,5,6,7). There is no Listener archetype anywhere in the repo -- `git ls-files | grep -i listen` returns only CREATURE_BEHAVIOR_CONTRACT.md, and src/game/creatures/ contains exactly one file. Creature.sense() returns [] (line 708) and Creature.behave() is empty (line 710). Everything in section 10.1 -- acoustic sense, 40 dB(V) emission, corridor carving, patrol, the 16->6 dB listening window -- is unwritten.

Acoustic transmission (section 4.1) reproduces the contract's worked values to within 0.04 dB. Measured from a cruise emission of 46 dB(V) in open clear air: 300 m -> 36.46 (contract 36.5), 1000 m -> 26.00 (26.0), 3000 m -> 16.46 (16.5), 6000 m -> 10.44 (10.4), and 6000 m inside a full duct -> 24.66 (24.7).

Sense ranges fall out correctly from that formula, matching section 10.1 without being tuned to. Bisected the range where received == threshold: cruise 46 dB(V) at threshold 16 -> 3162 m (contract 'about 3.2 km'), at the listening threshold 6 -> 10000 m (contract '10 km'). The 3.2x factor the design leans on is exact.
visibilityM(rho) matches the contract's sanity table: rho 0/0.25/0.5/0.75/1 -> 4000 / 986.4 / 243.2 / 60.0 / 14.8 m vs the stated 4000/987/244/60/15.

ductFromField reproduces section 2.3 verbatim and is not degenerate on the real cloud field. Unit checks: grad 0 -> 0; grad 0.002 at rho 0.1 -> 1.0; the same strong gradient inside a dense core (rho 0.95) -> 0. Sampled 400 points on GAME.clouds around the ship: 11% non-zero, p95 = 0.602, max 1.0 -- so ducts do occur naturally, and a p95 duct drops the spreading exponent from 20 to 15.2.

The attention integrator matches section 5.4's headline number. Drove a probe creature with excess held at exactly 0.4 and Listener constants (fill 0.12, decay 0.012): UNAWARE->COMMITTED in 19.1 s, against the contract's stated 19 s.

The escalation ladder walks one rung per transition and writes exactly one DetectionEvent per rung, never a jump. Log from that run: 5.20 UNAWARE->ALERT, 9.30 ALERT->SEARCHING, 14.50 SEARCHING->TRACKING, 19.10 TRACKING->COMMITTED. transitionCount() == 4.
The state machine converges. Swept all 5 states x 201 attention values (1005 cases) calling _resolveStates twice: 0 cases where the second call changed the state. It settles in one tick.

Hysteresis genuinely suppresses chatter. Parked attention on each of the four entry thresholds and alternated percept/no-percept every sense tick for 10 s: 0 state flips at ALERT, SEARCHING, TRACKING and COMMITTED.

The propagation delay is real and observable -- this is the design intent landing. Recorded a 70 dB(V) burst at t=100-102 against a 46 dB(V) cruise floor, then read the recorder as a 3 km listener would: nothing until t=109, then received jumps to 40.46 dB at t=110 (emitted at t=101) and falls back to 16.46 dB at t=112. That is a 9.1 s lag against soundDelayS(3000) = 9.09 s. You are heard for something you did nine seconds ago.

False-positive rate is correct, including the medium scaling. Measured over 200k sense ticks x 6 seeds: mean 0.0200 Hz against the contract's 0.02 base (per-seed 0.0192/0.0209/0.0215/0.0181/0.0204/0.0201). With section 5.3's acoustic mediumFactor of 2.0*g at g=1: 0.058 Hz vs the expected 0.060. I first measured 0.0171 on a single seed and re-ran across seeds rather than report it -- it was noise, not a bug.

azimuth and azimuthDir are exact inverses: max round-trip error 2.22e-16 rad over 64 bearings. (Measured as a round trip against a locally constructed direction, not against a world axis, per the project's lesson 1.)

Per-creature RNG isolation works. Two creatures handed the same parent Rng produce different false-positive sequences, because Rng.fork (rng.js:88) calls this.next() and advances the parent. I checked this rather than trusting the comment at line 59.

Cost is inside the section 8 budget. One 8-sample path integral over the real cloud field: 0.0429 ms on a cold cache, 0.0053 ms warm. Six creatures at one path each = 0.26 ms cold against the 1.0 ms AI budget.

gaps.what: The Listener does not exist. This module is the base class only -- no archetype implements sense() or behave(), so nothing in the project can ever produce a percept. Priority 4's actual deliverable is unwritten.
gaps.fix: Write src/game/creatures/listener.js as `class Listener extends Creature`. sense() must: compute distance to ship, reject beyond FAR_PLANE, read the signature history at the sound delay for that distance, call pathTerms into `this._terms`, call acousticReceived + acousticBearingSigma, perturb the bearing by sigma from this.rngSense, and return one percept (plus rollFalsePositive with mediumFactor 2.0*g_local). behave() must implement the patrol/carve and the per-state closing speeds from the 10.1 table. Also needs the 100-160 s silence window that drops currentThreshold() from 16 to 6 for 18-26 s -- currentThreshold() (line 546) exists as the override point and is currently a constant.

gaps.what: Nothing ever sets simLevel, so no creature ever senses. It defaults to 'reduced' (line 525) and update() gates sensing on fullySimulated (line 556). promotionRadius is computed at line 520 (16800 m for a FAR_PLANE sensor) and read by nothing; logPromotion (line 661) is called by nothing.

gaps.what: SignatureRecorder stores no position, so createSignatureView's fallback always fires: positionExact is false on every percept and transmission distance has to be computed from where the ship is NOW, not where it was when the sound was made. The delay is therefore observable in emission but not in geometry -- a ship that moves 500 m during a 9 s flight time is still ranged from its current position.
gaps.fix: The module documents this honestly at lines 300-315 and degrades correctly rather than lying. Either add x/y/z to SignatureRecorder's channel set (3 floats on a 14 KB buffer, as the comment proposes) or accept it and keep positionExact in the log.

bugs.problem: De-escalation from COMMITTED lands in SEARCHING and then immediately re-escalates to TRACKING inside the same sense tick, defeating the contract's explicit rule. Line 611 correctly picks SEARCHING as the down target, but line 612's `continue` re-enters the loop, where line 604 sees attention (0.736-) still >= STATE_ENTRY[TRACKING] (0.70) and promotes straight back up. The net observable transition is COMMITTED->TRACKING, which section 6 forbids by name. The bug is not really the `continue`: the exit line for COMMITTED (0.736) and the entry line for TRACKING (0.70) are only 0.036 apart, which at the Listener's 0.012/s decay is 3 seconds, so simply breaking after a down-step would still put the creature back in TRACKING almost at once. Honouring the rule requires the COMMITTED->SEARCHING transition to also drop attention below TRACKING's entry.
bugs.evidence: Drove a probe to COMMITTED, set attention to 0.92 and cut the stimulus. State trace: `t=15.4 att=0.7352 COMMITTED->TRACKING`, then `t=30.1 TRACKING->SEARCHING`. The creature never hunts the area -- it spends 14.7 more seconds tracking. The detection log shows the mechanism as two events at an identical timestamp: `t=15.40 COMMITTED->SEARCHING ch=decay att=0.7352` followed by `t=15.40 SEARCHING->TRACKING ch=decay att=0.7352`. Isolated it to a single call: state=COMMITTED, attention=0.7359, one _resolveStates -> ends in TRACKING having emitted both events. Note the second is an ESCALATION stamped channel 'decay', because logEvent (line 634) infers the channel from a null cause. Swept all attentions: exactly the band [0.700, 0.735] mis-lands in TRACKING -- which is precisely the band a continuously decaying creature must pass through, so in play it fires every time.

bugs.problem: createSignatureView.sampleAt(t) forwards its argument straight into history(t), and its docstring (lines 347, 300-317) defines that argument as an absolute sim time -- 'What the ship was emitting at t'. The only history implementation in the project is SignatureRecorder.at (src/game/signature.js:393), whose parameter is an AGE IN SECONDS ('What the ship was emitting ageSec ago'). pick() at line 321-322 binds it as the history source. The two conventions are mirror images, and nothing type-checks the difference.
bugs.evidence: Built a real SignatureRecorder, ran it to t=60 s, then called view.sampleAt(50.91) -- the absolute time a 3 km listener should read per the docstring. It returned the sample from simTime 9.0, i.e. 42 seconds wrong, mirrored about the present. The age convention view.sampleAt(9.09) returned simTime 51.0, which is correct. Worse, the recorder only spans 300 s: at t=400 s the absolute-time call returned null at every distance tested (300 m -> passed 399.09 -> null; 3000 m -> 390.91 -> null; 6000 m -> 381.82 -> null; 12000 m -> 363.64 -> null), because at() computes back = round(ageSec*hz) and rejects back >= count. A Listener wired per the docstring is deaf for the first five minutes in a scrambled way, then permanently and silently deaf.

bugs.problem: The derived-field cache is not deterministic, contradicting both its own comment and contract 2.1. derive() keys on quantised position and quantised time (line 213), but the values it stores are computed from source.densityAt/flowAt at whatever internal advection state the CloudSystem happens to be in when the entry is first created (lines 221-230). Time is in the key but not in the computation, so two calls with identical (x,y,z,t) return different answers depending on cache warmth. Density escapes this because line 247 samples it live -- which makes it worse: a returned MediumSample can carry a fresh density alongside a duct derived from a field state up to cellS=1.0 s old.
bugs.evidence: Probed a dense point (x=3353, y=850, z=1573, density 0.609) on the live GAME.clouds, sampled at t=5.0, then advanced field.shapeAdvect/weatherAdvect by 900 m and re-sampled at the SAME t=5.0. Warm cache returned {density 0.15701, duct 0.93605, turbulence 1.0}. A freshly built medium given the identical query returned {density 0.15701, duct 0.98438, turbulence 0.416}. Turbulence differs by 2.4x for the same (x,y,z,t). The comment at lines 194-196 claims it 'returns bit-identical values whether or not it happens to be warm -- a cache that changes results under replay is worse than no cache'; that is false as written. Contract 2.1 requires purity because 'the capture harness depends on two calls at the same sim time producing identical results, and so does every replay of a detection', and section 12 requires an identical detection log on replay.

bugs.problem: countingMedium counts calls to sample(), not field evaluations, so it under-reports the section 8 budget by roughly 8x. Each cold sample() costs 1 densityAt for the density plus, inside derive(), 4 densityAt for the tetrahedral gradient and 1 flowAt -- and CloudSystem.flowAt itself makes 3 more _densityCloud evaluations internally (clouds.js:878-880). The comment at lines 733-735 says the counter is what makes the cap measurable ('a cap nobody measures is a cap that has already been exceeded'), but MEDIUM_SAMPLE_BUDGET=32 compared against this counter permits 4 path integrals per sense tick, i.e. about 256 real field evaluations.
bugs.evidence: Instrumented GAME.clouds.densityAt and flowAt and ran one 8-sample pathTerms through countingMedium(createMedium(clouds)) on a cold cache: countingMedium reported 8, while the real field took 40 densityAt calls and 8 flowAt calls -- 64 density evaluations once flowAt's internal three are counted. A single sample() reported 1 against 5 real densityAt + 1 flowAt. The cache does amortise this in steady state (0.0429 ms cold vs 0.0053 ms warm per path), so the budget is not actually being blown today -- but the instrument cannot tell you that, which is the bug.

bugs.problem: this._terms is allocated and then never written by anything in the base class, so every DetectionEvent reports rho_mean/u_mean/q_mean/g_mean as 0. logEvent copies it verbatim at lines 648-653. Section 7's requirement is not just that a transition writes a record but that the record explains itself -- the contract's worked example turns on 'through rho 0.02 / duct 0.81', which is the clause that says why it was heard at six kilometres. pathTerms takes a dst argument that would make this work, but nothing in the base class passes this._terms and nothing checks that an archetype did.
bugs.evidence: Ran a probe creature to COMMITTED and read the third log event: medium came back {rho_mean: 0, u_mean: 0, q_mean: 0, g_mean: 0}, and formatEvent rendered `t=10.6  Listener#0  SEARCHING->TRACKING  acoustic  emitted 46.0, transmitted 40.0 at 5980 m through rho 0.00 / duct 0.00, threshold 16.0` -- structurally the contract's sentence with the explanatory half zeroed out. Confirmed _terms is still at its constructor values after 20 s of sensing.

bugs.problem: createMedium validates that the source has densityAt but then calls source.flowAt unconditionally at line 230, so a density-only source passes the guard and throws on first sample. The guard and the requirement disagree.
bugs.evidence: createMedium({ densityAt: () => 0.2 }).sample(0,0,0,0) throws 'source.flowAt is not a function'. CloudSystem happens to satisfy both, so this only bites the synthetic worlds the header comment (lines 17-20) says the adapters exist to support.

integrationNeeds:
main.js is currently 100% clean of this layer -- no import, and GAME has no creatures/detectionLog/signature key. Wiring is not a one-liner because the thing to wire does not exist yet: write src/game/creatures/listener.js first (see the blocking gap). Given that, main.js must do the following.

IMPORTS (add to the block at main.js lines 14-24):
  import { Signature } from './game/signature.js';
  import { createMedium, countingMedium, createSignatureView, formatEvent, STATE, soundDelayS } from './game/creatures/creature.js';
  import { Listener } from './game/creatures/listener.js';

CONSTRUCTION (once at boot, near where `clouds` and `ship` are made):
  const signature = new Signature({ medium: clouds });
  const sigView   = createSignatureView(signature.recorder);   // NOT signature itself -- Signature has no sampleAt/at/historyAt, so createSignatureView(signature) yields hasHistory:false and silently degrades to live-only, which destroys the propagation delay. Verified.
  const medium    = countingMedium(createMedium(clouds));
  const creatures = [ new Listener({ id:0, rng: rng.fork(RNG_TAG.LISTENER), senseOffset:0,  position:{...}, fillRate:0.12, decayRate:0.012, memorySec:240, threshold:16, saturation:60, falsePositiveBase:0.02, longestSenseRange:FAR_PLANE }) ];
  Give each creature a DIFFERENT senseOffset in 0..11 -- that stagger is the sensing latency per section 5.2, and identical offsets both spike the cost and remove the latency.

PER FIXED STEP, inside update(dt) at 120 Hz, in this order:
  1. signature.update(dt, ship, systems)  -- must run BEFORE the creatures, or they read a recorder that is one step stale.
  2. loop.perf.begin('ai')
  3. Promotion pass (nothing in creature.js does this and creatures never sense without it): for each creature compute vdist(c.position, ship.position); the nearest <=6 inside c.promotionRadius get c.simLevel='full', the rest 'reduced'; on any change call c.logPromotion(ctx, from, to, dist).
  4. const ctx = { tick: loop.tick, t: loop.simTime, medium, signature: sigView, shipPos: ship.position, shipVel: ship.velocity };
     Reuse one ctx object; do not allocate per creature per step.
  5. for (const c of creatures) c.update(loop.stepSec, loop.tick, ctx);
     ctx.medium is mandatory -- _senseTick dereferences ctx.medium.samplesTaken unconditionally and throws without it.
  6. One-COMMITTED enforcement (contract 6, unimplemented anywhere -- I measured 3 simultaneous COMMITTED): if more than one c.state === STATE.COMMITTED, keep the highest attention and push the rest to SEARCHING via _transition so the demotion is logged.
  7. loop.perf.end('ai')  -- section 8 budgets creature AI at 1.0 ms and section 12 requires it measured with perf.begin/end('ai'), not assumed.

HOW THE LISTENER MUST READ THE PAST (this is where bug 2 bites): call sigView.sampleAt(soundDelayS(d), ship.position) with an AGE, not sigView.sampleAt(t - soundDelayS(d), ...) as the docstring instructs. The absolute-time form returns null at every distance once simTime > 300 s. Fix the adapter to `history(ctx.t - t)` (or make the Listener pass an age) and pick one convention in the docstring.

RENDERING: creature.js deliberately has no Three.js and holds only {x,y,z}. main.js owns the mesh -- create one per creature at boot, and in render() copy creature.position into mesh.position. A 240 m body at FAR_PLANE=12000 needs its own LOD/near-far handling; nothing here helps with that.

AUDIO: src/audio/language.js already exports CreatureVoice and CREATURES.listener. main.js must feed it {state, attention, distance, bearing} per frame; creature.js emits none of that on its own and the section 10.1 call schedule (every 40-90 s, silent while ALERT+) has to live in the Listener's behave().

GAME SURFACE (section 7 requires it by name -- 'Exposed as GAME.detectionLog(), returning the last 64'):
  creatures,
  signature,
  detectionLog: () => creatures.flatMap(c => c.detectionLog()).sort((a,b) => a.simTime - b.simTime).slice(-64),
  detectionLines: () => GAME.detectionLog().map(formatEvent),
  creatureStates: () => creatures.map(c => c.snapshot()),
Without at least detectionLog on GAME there is no way to run section 12's pass condition ('every state transition in a 900 s recorded session has a matching DetectionEvent, zero exceptions').

DETERMINISM CAVEAT: GAME.seek()/GAME.capture() jump the sim. The derived-field cache in createMedium returns different duct/turbulence for the same (x,y,z,t) depending on warmth (bug 3), so a detection log replayed after a seek will not reproduce. Fix that before relying on captures as creature regression baselines.

complete: Uniform packing is correct and space-correct. Verified by driving writeUniforms() against a mock uniform object: uLightPos.w = 1/radius (55 m -> 0.01818), uLightCol.rgb = colour * intensity ([5, 4.7, 4.1] for the lamp), uLightCol.a = the per-frame shadow grant (1 for the lamp, 0.45 for the thruster, 0 for the six that lost the budget), uLightPar.y = range^2 (1509475 for the lamp = 1228.6^2). Positions are rebased by `origin` (clouds.js passes this.origin, and clouds.js:771 fills _v3 from camera.getWorldPosition, so the cull runs in world space and the packing in cloud space — both correct).

The omni-as-spot encoding works as claimed. OMNI_COS_OUTER = -2.0 / OMNI_COS_INNER = -1.2 are written straight through, and smoothstep(-2.0, -1.2, dot) saturates to 1 for every direction, so an omni light takes the same branch-free path as a spot. Confirmed in the packed uniforms: omni lights carry dir.w = -2, par.x = -1.2.

The inner>=outer guard at line 251 works. Feeding cone {inner:1.2, outer:0.30} produced cosOuter 0.95534 and cosInner 0.95563 — still correctly ordered for smoothstep, so a mis-authored cone degrades to a hairline edge instead of producing a NaN or an inverted cone.

prepare() is deterministic and its bounded set is a pure function of the scene. With 22 registered lights, two consecutive prepare() calls returned the byte-identical order [lamp, thr, bio1, bio2, bio0, bio3, bio4, bio5] and active.length capped at 8.

The shadow budget is enforced on the default construction path. With 22 lights registered and 8 active, exactly 2 carried _shadowThisFrame > 0 (debugSummary().shadowed === 2), matching MAX_SHADOWED_LIGHTS.

The occlusion march is real and load-bearing — it just needs density to show. With the camera inside cloud (densityAt = 0.6004 at the camera, measured), a shipLamp at intensity 12 differed from lamp-off by meanAbs 8.24 / maxAbs 577 (of 765), and shadow:1 vs shadow:0 differed by meanAbs 1.996 / maxAbs 212 — roughly a quarter of the lamp's whole contribution is being removed by occlusion. shadowRange 600 vs 40 differed by meanAbs 0.363 / maxAbs 50, so that knob is live too. An earlier identical test in clear air showed a 0.000 difference, which was a null environment and not a bug — I checked before reporting it.

signature() arithmetic is correct. A registry holding shipLamp(intensity 5) + shipLamp(intensity 5, on:false) + bioluminescence(intensity 99) returns exactly 5 — off lights excluded, non-signature lights excluded, and it is sum(intensity * max(colour)) as documented.

The registry is correctly hooked into the render path. clouds.js:797-798 calls lights.prepare(this._v3, u.uCamFwd.value) then lights.writeUniforms(u, this.origin) inside _writeCameraUniforms, per drawn frame rather than per fixed step. Nothing in main.js needs to call either.
Reachable at runtime as GAME.clouds.lights — confirmed on a fresh page load (hasLights: true).

gaps.what: The module has no content. On a fresh page load GAME.clouds.lights holds exactly 4 lights — storm/0..storm/3, all on:false, all intensity 0 — and lights.signature() returns 0. Nothing anywhere in the repo calls shipLamp(), thrusterPlume() or bioluminescence(); grep across every .js and .html finds them only inside lights.js itself. Every god-ray source the art direction names as required (ship exterior lights, thrusters, creature bioluminescence) is absent at runtime. The module is a correct engine with no fuel in it.
gaps.fix: main.js must add and drive at least the ship lamp and the thruster plume — see integrationNeeds for the exact calls. This is ~15 lines and is the single highest-value change in the whole audit.

gaps.what: MAX_MARCH_LIGHTS = 8 is roughly 2.7x more lights than the shader can afford, and the module's own header says the opposite ("A scene may hold any number of lights and the shader cost does not move"). Measured with clouds.benchPass (EXT_disjoint_timer_query_webgl2, not gl.finish), 1280x720, quality high, camera inside density-0.60 cloud, lights within range of most march samples: 0 lights 2.479 ms; then 4.179, 5.964, 7.493, 9.070, 10.657, 12.208, 13.691, 15.216 ms for n = 1..8. That is a dead-straight +1.57 ms per light. The 7 ms volumetric budget is blown at n = 3 and exceeded 2.2x at n = 8 (benchPass reported withinBudget: false).
gaps.fix: Either drop MAX_MARCH_LIGHTS to 2-3 and re-tune priority so the lamp and the nearest event always win, or make the shader's analytic path cheaper. Do not spend the saving on more shadow marches — see the next item, they are already free.

gaps.what: The cost model in the header comment is inverted. It says occlusion "is the only part that costs texture fetches" and caps it at 2 for that reason. Measured: 8 lights with shadow forced to 0 cost 15.216 ms; the same 8 with the registry granting 2 shadow marches cost 15.257 ms. The shadow marches are 0.04 ms of a 15.2 ms pass — 0.3%. MAX_SHADOWED_LIGHTS = 2 is buying nothing, and the budget is being spent entirely on the path the header calls free.
gaps.fix: Raise MAX_SHADOWED_LIGHTS (occlusion is what makes a beam read as volume) and cut MAX_MARCH_LIGHTS instead. Then rewrite the header comment — it is currently misleading anyone who tunes this next.

gaps.what: The signature coupling that justifies the module's existence is not wired, and the two ends do not share units. lights.js:277 signature() returns a radiance sum in the CLOUD_PALETTE scale (shipLamp 5.0, lamp+plume 6.5). signature.js:757 _photic() sums bus.records[].photicLm in LUMENS plus a hard-coded plume term, with SIG.caps.photic = 60000 and SIG.exposureRef.photic = 40000. Nothing imports lights.js into signature.js; LightRegistry.signature() has zero callers in the repo. The ShipSystems class that _photic() reads its records from (signature.js:587 JSDoc, :770) does not exist anywhere in the repo either.
gaps.fix: A ShipSystems emitter must convert the registry's radiance total into lumens and push it as photicLm. The conversion constant is exactly the kind of number this project has been burned by three times — measure it against the anchor table in signature.js rather than picking one, and record the measurement next to it.

gaps.what: A low, cold, high-contrast key with deep shadow separation is NOT reachable through this module's parameters. Measured on a 320x180 frame: with no local lights, luminance p05 = 92.7, p50 = 119.2, p95 = 244.2, p95-p05 contrast = 151.4. bugs.problem: The range cull tests the CAMERA's distance to the light, but the shader applies the matching window per MARCH SAMPLE. Those are different points. A light in front of the camera and just beyond `range` still has march samples passing through its core (r -> 0, attenuation -> 1), so the CPU throws away light the GPU would have drawn at full strength, and it does so as a hard on/off switch at a sphere in world space.
bugs.evidence: Live measurement in the running game. Probe = bioluminescence(intensity 6.0), range() = 3286.3 m, placed along the camera forward axis. At 3283 m (0.999 x range) prepare() keeps it (inSet: true) and the frame mean RGB rises by +5.943 / +8.278 / +7.720. At 3288 m (1.0005 x range) prepare() drops it (inSet: false) and the frame changes by exactly +0.000 / +0.000 / +0.000. I then monkeypatched prepare() to append the same light past the cull at that same 3288 m and the shader drew +6.566 / +13.425 / +11.643. So five metres of camera movement — 0.15% of the light's range — switches a clearly visible glow fully on and fully off. The comment at lines 132-135 claims 'The shader windows the falloff to zero exactly here, so this is not a visible edge'; that is true of a point sample at the light's own range, and false of the cull actually implemented. In game this means a bioluminescent creature (shipped range 1692.8 m) materialises its entire glow in one frame as it drifts toward the player, and a distant storm cell's ember phase (range ~1562 m at ember intensity, ~13 km during a stroke) is invisible until it strokes.

bugs.problem: MAX_MARCH_LIGHTS = 8 cannot be afforded, and the header comment at lines 14-28 asserts the opposite — 'the set handed to the GPU is bounded at MAX_MARCH_LIGHTS ... A scene may hold any number of lights and the shader cost does not move.' The cost moves linearly and steeply with the count, and it is the analytic path — the one the header calls cheap — that costs everything.
bugs.evidence: clouds.benchPass with EXT_disjoint_timer_query_webgl2 (NOT gl.finish, which reported 0.045 ms for every configuration and is the backend lie this project already documented), 1280x720, quality high, camera inside cloud at densityAt = 0.60, bioluminescence probes at intensity 4 so all are in range of most march samples. Volumetric median by light count: n=0 2.479 ms, n=1 4.179, n=2 5.964, n=3 7.493, n=4 9.070, n=5 10.657, n=6 12.208, n=7 13.691, n=8 15.216. Dead linear at +1.57 ms per light. The 7 ms volumetric budget is exceeded at n=3 and by 2.2x at n=8; benchPass itself returned withinBudget: false. Separately, 8 lights with shadow forced to 0 cost 15.216 ms against 15.257 ms with the registry's 2 shadow marches granted — a 0.04 ms difference, so the entire MAX_SHADOWED_LIGHTS mechanism is guarding a cost that does not exist while the real cost is unguarded.

bugs.problem: `this.maxShadowed = Math.min(maxShadowed, this.max)` clamps against the wrong constant. `max` is correctly clamped to MAX_MARCH_LIGHTS on the line above, but `maxShadowed` is clamped to `this.max` (8) instead of to MAX_SHADOWED_LIGHTS (2), so a caller can silently grant four times the documented shadow budget.
bugs.evidence: `new LightRegistry({ max: 99, maxShadowed: 99 })` returns max: 8 (correctly clamped) but maxShadowed: 8. After adding eight shipLamps and calling prepare(), eight of them carried _shadowThisFrame > 0 — four times the MAX_SHADOWED_LIGHTS of 2 that the comment at lines 50-52 says is 'affordable two at a time and not four'. Latent today because clouds.js:252 constructs with `new LightRegistry()` and takes the defaults, but it is a trap for the next caller, and the export MAX_SHADOWED_LIGHTS is currently a number the code does not enforce anywhere.

bugs.problem: `const n = Math.hypot(dst[0], dst[1], dst[2]) || 1;` guards against dividing by zero but lets a zero direction vector survive normalisation unchanged. A spot with direction [0,0,0] then emits nothing at all, while still consuming a march slot and still counting toward signature().
bugs.evidence: `add(shipLamp({ direction: [0,0,0] }))` leaves light.direction as [0,0,0] (measured). In the shader that makes the cone term smoothstep(cos(0.30), cos(0.13), dot(-L, vec3(0))) = smoothstep(0.9553, 0.9916, 0) = 0, so the lamp is black in every direction — yet prepare() still ranks and packs it, and signature() still reports 5.0. That is precisely the feedback loop the header at lines 30-35 says must never break: the ship broadcasts loudly and the player sees no beam. It is reachable the moment someone wires this in, because `Light.apply` only skips the field when `p.direction` is falsy, and a fresh `new THREE.Vector3()` — the natural thing to pass on frame 0 — is truthy with all components zero.

bugs.problem: `remove(id)` deletes from the Map but never splices `this.active`, so a light removed after prepare() and before writeUniforms() is still packed into the uniforms and still drawn for that frame.
bugs.evidence: add -> prepare -> remove -> writeUniforms against a mock uniform object returned registered: 0 but written: 1 and uLightCount: 1. Harmless on today's call order (clouds.js:797-798 runs prepare and writeUniforms back to back), but the moment creatures despawn on their own schedule a dead creature's lantern will flash for one frame at its last position — a false 'something is there' in a game whose entire dread mechanic is inference from partial light.

bugs.problem: The spot does not produce a shaft. Viewed along its own axis it renders as a flat, hard-edged, saturated white DISC that occludes the cloud behind it; viewed from the side it is a hard geometric wedge with radial streaking around the source. The mechanism is that along the beam axis dot(L, rd) is near-constant for every sample in the cone, so the phase term, the squared cone term and the integrated attenuation are all flat across the disc and the result saturates to white with no interior structure. This is the 'solid of revolution' artifact the shader comment claims to have cured by squaring the cone term; squaring softened it, it did not remove it.
bugs.evidence: I captured it: evidence/audit_lamp_shadow_on.png — shipLamp at intensity 12, aimed along the view axis, camera at densityAt 0.60 — is a clean white circle with a soft rim in the middle of the frame, no cone, no axial falloff, no density structure, and it hides a small cloud that is behind it. Compare evidence/audit_lamp_off.png, the identical frame with the lamp off. The previous agent's own evidence/gr_lamp_along.png shows the same disc more softly, and evidence/gr_lamp_side.png shows the side view as a solid white wedge with a dark radial fan behind the source. Note also that evidence/gr_lamp.png, filed as lamp evidence, contains no visible lamp contribution at all. The art direction's requirement that shafts 'bend around what is actually in the volume' is not met by this shape, even though the occlusion march underneath it demonstrably works.

   Passing `clouds` as the medium is verified to work with no adapter: CloudSystem.densityAt(x,y,z) and CloudSystem.flowAt(x,y,z,out) both match what Signature expects, flowAt fills and returns the out object, and driving through real cloud measurably moved densityFactor 1.000 -> 2.245 and thermal tau 90 -> 52.1 s.

3. PER-FRAME, inside update(dt), AFTER `ship.step(dt)` (line 142) and before `shipCam.update` (line 144):
   signature.update(dt, ship, systems);
   Order is load-bearing: _kinematics reads ship.velocity, ship.gLoad and ship.slipAngle, and flight.js only writes gLoad and slipAngle at the end of step() (lines 291-295). Calling before step() reads last frame's manoeuvre.
   main.js already samples clouds.flowAt and clouds.densityAt at the ship each frame (lines 128-130) for turbulence; Signature resamples them independently on a 30 Hz rota. The duplicate cost is negligible (whole update() measured at 0.0173 ms/step with both trail buffers full and the real medium attached, ~1.2% of the 3 ms update budget), so either share the sample or leave it.

4. FLOATING ORIGIN. main.js does not rebase yet, but Flight.rebase(offset) exists at flight.js:343. Whenever the rebase call site is added, `signature.rebase(offset)` must be called in the same place and with the same offset — trail parcels are stored in world space and will otherwise be stranded. Verified: sampleWake read 2.289 before and 2.289 after an 8880 m rebase, so the method is correct, it just has no caller.

   globalThis.GAME = { ..., ship, signature, systems,
     sig: () => signature.report(),
     sigBreakdown: (c) => signature.breakdown(c), ... }

6. EVENT HOOKS that currently have no caller anywhere in the repo:
   - signature.impact(severity) on any hull collision (sets the 110 dB transient and the +2.5 s-1 wake impulse; verified 106.6 dB at 0.1 s decaying to baseline by 3 s).
   - signature.dumpHeat(fraction, ship) for the emergency vent. Use this method, NOT bus.thermalDumpFraction — the bus path erases heat without shedding a decoy (bug above).

7. HUD/instrument rate limit: call signature.breakdown() / report() at 10 Hz or slower. Both allocate fresh arrays and objects on every call, and PERFORMANCE_BUDGET.md line 141 requires zero steady-state per-frame allocations. signature.values() is safe per-frame (returns a reused object; verified identity-stable).
